Job Roles & Responsibilities:

Responsible for managing and ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely financial reporting for one or more legal entities within the sub-region. The role supports statutory, regulatory, and corporate governance requirements while partnering closely with the CFO, Company Finance Manager, auditors, and key business stakeholders to deliver high-quality financial reporting and control.

Financial Reporting & Close Management

- Coordinate and oversee month-end, quarter-end, and year-end closing activities for assigned legal entities.

- Review journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, and financial statements to ensure completeness and accuracy.

- Support consolidation and reporting requirements for group and management reporting.

Statutory & Regulatory Compliance

- Prepare and coordinate statutory financial statements in collaboration with the Company Finance Manager.

- Ensure compliance with Companies Act, SEBI regulations, stock exchange reporting requirements, and other applicable statutory regulations.

Governance, Controls & Audit

- Drive timely closure of audit observations and implementation of corrective actions.

- Support risk assessment and control monitoring activities across the reporting process.

Business Partnering & Stakeholder Management

- Act as the primary finance interface for the Company Finance Manager, CFO, Corporate Finance, and external stakeholders.

- Partner with business teams to provide financial insights, accounting guidance, and reporting support.

- Support Board, Audit Committee, and leadership reporting requirements through preparation of high-quality financial analyses and presentations.

Performance Reporting & Continuous Improvement

- Support CFO and senior management with profitability analysis, margin reviews, working capital reporting, and quarterly board packs.

- Drive process standardization, automation, and reporting improvements through SKF Business Excellence and digital initiatives.

- Lead initiatives focused on improving reporting quality, compliance, efficiency, and control effectiveness.

- Actively contribute to finance transformation projects, ERP enhancements, and process optimization initiatives.

Experience

- Qualified Chartered Accountant (CA).

- 15+ years of progressive experience in Finance, Accounting, and Controllership functions.

- Demonstrated experience within:

- Financial Accounting & Reporting

- Financial Controlling

- Statutory Compliance

- Audit Management

- Corporate Governance

- Listed Company Reporting Environment

Competency Profile

- Solid experience in a listed company environment.

- In-depth knowledge of Ind AS, IFRS, Companies Act, and regulatory reporting requirements.

- Strong understanding of financial close, consolidation, and statutory reporting processes.

- Experience managing internal and external audits.

- Knowledge of Internal Financial Controls (IFC) and governance frameworks.

- Strong analytical, stakeholder management, and business partnering skills.

- Proven ability to identify and implement process improvements.

- Advanced ERP knowledge (SAP/S4HANA preferred).

- Strong communication, presentation, and board-reporting capabilities.

Role Success Criteria

- Timely and accurate financial, statutory, and regulatory reporting.

- Zero material audit findings and strong compliance adherence.

- Effective stakeholder engagement with CFO, auditors, and business leadership.

- Continuous improvement in reporting quality, controls, and automation.

- Demonstrates ownership, accountability, collaboration, and a strong team-first mindset.

- Supports the organization in maintaining high standards of governance expected of a listed entity.

We are seeking a qualified Chartered Accountant with 5-8 years of relevant experience to join our Consolidation team. The ideal candidate will support the end-to-end consolidation process for the group, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting across multiple entities. The role will involve consolidated financial reporting, foreign currency (FX) translation, goodwill calculation and accounting, Oracle/FCCS consolidation activities, and topside adjustment management. The candidate will also contribute to strengthening internal controls, improving consolidation processes, supporting audits, and ensuring key reporting deliverables are IPE compliant. This position requires strong technical accounting knowledge combined with effective stakeholder management, with regular interaction across regional controllers, entity finance teams, auditors, and other cross-functional stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities:
• Support the monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidation process for multiple global entities within the group using Oracle FCCS.
• Assist in timely and accurate preparation and review of consolidated financial statements out of Oracle FCCS and related reporting deliverables.
• Coordinate with regional controllers, External Reporting and Tax team to gather any financial information or supporting documentation as needed and also address any queries that they may have from time to time.
• Perform monthly goodwill reconciliation to ensure that workings are accurate, including acquisition-related adjustments, FX, or any other adjustments.
• Perform inter-company elimination review of dividends and investment/equity balances and resolve the differences by working with controllers.
• Prepare and monitor topside journal entries in Oracle/FCCS, including preparation/posting, validation, and appropriate supporting documentation.
• Review foreign currency (FX) translation of subsidiary financial statements, including validation of exchange rates, translation adjustments, and related consolidation impacts.
• Support in preparation and compilation of variance/flux analysis commentaries of consolidated BS and PL.
• Assist in designing, implementing, and strengthening SOX controls and IPE documentation over the consolidation and Financial Statement Close Process (FSCP).
• Support timely resolution and closure of internal and external audit queries relating to consolidation, controls, and supporting documentation.
• Drive close acceleration by collaborating with key stakeholders, including regional controllers, on a continuous basis.
• Perform sub-consolidations for tax purposes and address any ad-hoc data queries received from time to time.
• Participate in ad hoc assignments, automation initiatives, system enhancements, and other consolidation/process-improvement projects.

Requirements:
• Qualified CA/CPA with 5-8 years of relevant experience, with significant exposure to financial consolidation and GAAP reporting, preferably US GAAP.
• Strong knowledge of the complete consolidation cycle and concepts including intercompany eliminations, FX, goodwill, acquisition accounting, etc.
• Strong understanding of internal/SOX controls for FSCP process.
• Exposure to consolidation tools like Hyperion, Oracle/FCCS, Tagetik, etc.
• Proficiency in MS Office, with advanced Excel skills.
• Working knowledge of ERP systems like SAP, QAD, etc.
• Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate effectively in a dynamic environment.
• Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to effectively communicate, collaborate, and influence stakeholders across teams and geographies.
• Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
